"SPIRIT RHYTHM": A KANAWANA COLLECTIVE ON A MONTREAL STAGE, NOVEMBER 1993
The McGill Daily, Culture section, Vol. 83 No. 46, Thursday 25 November 1993.
Internet Archive item McGillLibrary-mcgill-daily-culture-v83-n046-november-25-
1993-13865. Found 2026-09-07 by the whole-corpus sweep of 9,890 McGill student
publication items under p_479.

=====================================================================
THE PASSAGE
=====================================================================

  "Do it yourself, environmental style / Contemporary dance and music at the
  Hive / BY JULIE CRYSLER

  Spirit Rhythm is an evening of contemporary dance and music that has been
  eight weeks in the making. THE MAJORITY OF THE MEMBERS OF THE AS YET UNNAMED
  COLLECTIVE KNOW EACH OTHER FROM CAMP KANAWANA NEAR ST. SAUVER [sic].
  ALORANI MARTIN, one of the dancers and choreograph[e]rs, explains that
  Spirit Rhythm was a project that 'started small and grew'. There are now
  eight members in the collective. They will be performing music by SEAN DAY
  and HARTLEY WYNBERG at the Hive. ...

  Spirit Rhythm has a definite folksy, environmentalist appeal, with acoustic
  guitar and Indigo [G]irls-type harmonies. It's quite engaging, and the
  dancing is excellent.

  '**A lot of my songs are about the earth. I USED TO WORK WITH A NATURALIST,
  MOSTLY IN KANAWANA. WE USED TO DO AN "EARTH VALUES" PROGRAM** and I think
  the other people who worked on the show are on the same wavelength as far as
  those things go,' says SEAN DAY.

  The show is being held at the Hive, which is actually a warehouse [l]oft
  that is home to five people. They rent the place out for shows like this,
  but mostly for raves and ..."

=====================================================================
WHY IT MATTERS, IN ORDER
=====================================================================

1. SEAN DAY, TWELVE YEARS BEFORE THE DIRECTORSHIP, DESCRIBING WHAT HE DID AT
   THE CAMP. people/sean-day.md has him as Director of Camp YMCA Kanawana and
   Regional Director of Camps for the Quebec YMCAs from 2005 to April 2023,
   and says he "grew up at Camp Kanawana and rose from camper to counsellor to
   director" -- WITHOUT DATING ANY OF THAT. Here he is in November 1993,
   speaking for himself, placing his own work at the camp in the past tense
   and naming the programme he ran: "I used to work with a naturalist, mostly
   in Kanawana. We used to do an 'earth values' program."

2. "EARTH VALUES" WAS A KANAWANA PROGRAMME IN OR BEFORE 1993. This project
   knows the phrase only from the other end: traditions/environmental-history.md
   has CHRIS ADAM, the camp's naturalist figure and the 2017 Pip Award
   recipient, as Executive Director of the EARTHVALUES INSTITUTE, a non-profit
   with a "Nature as Mentor" philosophy -- a later, separate organisation.
   THE PHRASE WAS IN USE AT THE CAMP FIRST, and Day says he ran the programme
   "with a naturalist".

   THE NATURALIST IS NOT NAMED IN THE ARTICLE. Chris Adam is the obvious
   candidate -- he created Kanawana's Nature Awareness programme in 1980 and
   is the naturalist this project knows -- but Day does not name him and
   nothing here does. IT IS A STRONG READING AND NOT A DOCUMENT.

3. THE CAMP PRODUCED A WORKING ARTISTIC COLLECTIVE. Eight people, most of whom
   "know each other from Camp Kanawana", eight weeks of rehearsal, a paid
   warehouse venue, and a reviewer who thought the dancing excellent. This
   project has almost nothing on what campers and staff made together AFTER
   camp, and this is a dated, reviewed instance of it.

4. THREE NAMES NEW TO THIS PROJECT: ALORANI MARTIN (dancer and choreographer),
   HARTLEY WYNBERG (music, with Day), and JULIE CRYSLER (the reviewer). None
   occurs anywhere in the wiki, the KB or the source index, checked.

=====================================================================
WHAT IT IS NOT
=====================================================================

It is a review of a dance show, not a document about the camp. It gives no
years for Day's camp work, no name for the naturalist, no content for the
"earth values" programme beyond its name, and no roster of the collective
beyond three people. THE PHRASE "USED TO" IS THE ONLY DATING INSTRUMENT IN IT.

And the shape matches the Georgian sweep exactly, which is worth noting because
it is now twice: a student newspaper's contact with this camp is NOT reporting
about it. It is an advertisement, a retirement notice, or -- here -- a review
of something the camp's people went on to make.
